idle: Nobody in. I could count the till again.
Quiet. Too quiet for a weekday.
I have dusted this shelf three times now.
The bell has not rung in an hour.
I could close for ten minutes and nobody would know.
Everyone must be at the market today.
The clock on the wall is slower than usual.
If nobody comes, at least nobody complains.
I know every crack in this counter by now.
Should I put a sign in the window? A sale, maybe.
Somebody looked in and walked on. Story of my day.
Still paid by the hour. Customers or not.
Lean on the counter. Watch the street. Wait.
The till drawer sticks again. Nobody to open it for anyway.
closing: That is my shift. Somebody else's turn.
Till counted, counter wiped, I am off.
Feet up at home in half an hour.
Done. Not one minute more behind that counter.
Good day, all told. Better than yesterday.
Hand over the keys, and home.
Long shift. Every bit of it in my back.
Let the next one deal with the late crowd.
The shelves are somebody else's problem now.
Off the clock. Do not ask me for anything.
